title: What stack should you use for vibe coding?

beats.purpose: Open with a clear recommendation and remove stack confusion.
beats.voiceover: If you're vibe coding a web app, you probably don't need a complicated tech stack.
beats.onScreenText: The vibe coding stack I would use
beats.visualPlaceholder: Strong opening frame. Show a finished modern web app in the browser next to Cursor or Claude Code with the project open.
beats.notes: Lead with simplicity and a concrete recommendation.

beats.purpose: Show why choosing too many tools makes AI app building harder.
beats.voiceover: The more frameworks, backend tools, and services you add, the more chances your AI has to generate code that does not work together.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show a messy stack list with multiple frontend frameworks, backend frameworks, databases, auth providers, and hosting platforms.
beats.notes: Make the stack feel unnecessarily complicated.

beats.voiceover: For most web apps, I would start with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Supabase, and Vercel.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show a clean stack overview with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase, and Vercel.
beats.notes: Keep this frame simple. This is the core recommendation.

beats.voiceover: Next.js gives you the app structure, TypeScript keeps the code safer, and Tailwind makes it fast to build the UI.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show a Next.js project open in the code editor and the matching dashboard UI running in the browser.
beats.notes: Connect the technologies directly to something visible.

beats.purpose: Explain why Supabase simplifies the backend.
beats.voiceover: Then Supabase handles your database and authentication, so you don't need to build a separate backend for a simple app.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show the Supabase dashboard with Authentication open, then switch to a database table containing example app data.
beats.notes: Show both auth and database so the benefit is concrete.

beats.voiceover: And when the app works locally, deploy the Next.js project to Vercel.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show the project running locally, followed by the same app opened from a deployed Vercel URL.

beats.purpose: Show how the stack works inside a real vibe coding workflow.
beats.voiceover: Now I can ask Cursor or Claude Code to build a dashboard with login, create a projects table in Supabase, and connect everything together.
beats.onScreenText: Build the feature with one clear prompt
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show Cursor or Claude Code receiving a prompt: Build a Next.js dashboard with Supabase authentication and a projects table. Then show generated files appearing.
beats.notes: The prompt should be readable and tied directly to the recommended stack.

beats.purpose: Prove that the full stack works together.
beats.voiceover: The result is a real app where I can log in, create a project, refresh the page, and the data is still there.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show the finished app: sign in, create a new project, refresh the browser, then show the same project still visible and the matching row inside Supabase.
beats.notes: This is the strongest proof beat. Show persistence, not just a pretty UI.

beats.purpose: Summarize why this stack fits vibe coding.
beats.voiceover: You get frontend, auth, database, and deployment with a stack that AI coding tools already understand very well.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show the finished app next to a compact summary of frontend, authentication, database, and deployment.
beats.notes: Focus on reduced complexity and a complete working app.

beats.purpose: Give the viewer a clear reason to watch the next video.
beats.voiceover: Follow and I'll show you the exact prompt I would use to build this stack from zero.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show Cursor or Claude Code with an empty prompt box next to the finished app.
beats.notes: Tie the CTA directly to a practical follow-up video.
